_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions) and For Fable (engineering). Items are DELETED when done, never left checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-13 · SkyTop — the answer looked right, and five confirmed matches were being dropped.
_status: Two things were quietly broken and both are now fixed and live. First: when Sierra was asked whether Cerritos should adopt the POST police-academy credit, she told faculty to 'go check your catalog' for five courses Cerritos already teaches — and which we already held, matched by C-ID, the statewide course-identity standard. The data was right the whole time; the answer was drowning it. Two causes: a limit that trimmed one half of the results but left the other half unbounded (3,807 rows of 'here is what other colleges did' against 9 rows of 'here is your own matching course'), and peer colleges' own phrasing being treated as if it were a real recommendation — so POST's TEN recommendations became FORTY-THREE, most of them phantoms that each honestly reported 'no match'. Second: the Cerritos ironworker question Sam has reported three times. He asked as a student would — 'I have a journey worker license as Iron and Steel worker' — and got nothing, against thirteen real Cerritos ironworker credentials. Three separate causes, including that we never searched the awarding body (three of those thirteen are only findable through 'Field Ironworkers Local 416' — their own titles say nothing about iron) and that the word 'iron' was never actually asked, having fallen off the end of an internal list. That one is not a Cerritos quirk: 90% of our credentials have an issuer carrying a word that appears nowhere in the title. Sam has also set the direction for the next piece — a Common CR Reference, matched on many factors the way the CCR is, with C-ID as one signal among several rather than the key.

items.text: Re-ask the ironworker question — 'I have a journey worker license as Iron and Steel worker. What CPL can I get here?' — with Cerritos selected. She should now name the Ironworker Apprenticeship credentials, including the three whose own titles say nothing about ironwork (FIW Orientation, Foreman Training, Post Tensioning 3). This is the one you have reported three times; it is the acceptance test.

Re-ask the Cerritos POST question. All six C-ID matches should now appear (AJ 101, 102, 103, 104, 107, 222) instead of 'check your catalog'. The line worth watching is Physical Training and Health Education — it shares a C-ID with Intro to Administration of Justice, so it is deliberately flagged as a mismatch rather than quietly resolved.

Confirm the matching factors for the Common CR Reference. You named title, course name and number, course description, subject, 'etc.' — the etc. is doing real work and it has been recorded as illustrative, not final. Worth pinning down before anything gets built.

You flagged 'Wrong contact information for RCC' when asking about Riverside firefighter CPL. Confirming what the right contact is would let this be fixed — MAP is read-only for us, so it would land as a proposed fill rather than a change to MAP itself.

Someone asked, after a good answer about students served statewide, whether they could export or download it to share with constituents. Worth deciding whether Sierra answers get a copy/export affordance — it was a thumbs-up, so the ask came from a satisfied user.

Both defects this run were found in an answer Sam pasted back, not in the code — the database function and the renderer each verified clean on their own, and the loss was between them. Sessions cannot reach Sierra from the sandbox, so the live answer is the only place this class of bug is visible. Ask for one.

Scope the Common CR Reference against how the CCR actually matches courses, before building. Starting numbers: 2,344 distinct recommendation wordings, and only about 7% of them collapse by tidying punctuation and casing — so this is curation work, not text cleanup. Only 17% carry a C-ID at all.
12 credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but are missing from Sierra's credential table entirely, so she cannot find them at all. Carried over from the previous session.

The college profile data Sierra reads has not been refreshed since 25 June, and the exhibit corpus still covers only 59 of 123 colleges. A college we cannot see is a blind spot, never a zero — and this run is a reminder of how expensive a false zero is.
